units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
There are many who cannot afford to marry, sir.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Yes, that is just what I say.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: But they may have a home for all that. And several of them have, as a matter of fact; and very pleasant, well-ordered homes they are, too.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: MRS. ALVING follows with breathless interest; nods, but says nothing.
But I'm not talking of bachelors' quarters. By a "home" I understand the home of a family, where a man lives with his wife and children.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes; or with his children and his children's mother.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Starts; clasps his hands.
But, good heavens--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Well?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Lives with--his children's mother!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes. Would you have him turn his children's mother out of doors?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Then it is illicit relations you are talking of! Irregular marriages, as people call them!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: I have never noticed anything particularly irregular about the life these people lead.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: But how is it possible that a--a young man or young woman with any decency of feeling can endure to live in that way?--in the eyes of all the world!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: What are they to do? A poor young artist--a poor girl--marriage costs a great deal. What are they to do?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: What are they to do? Let me tell you, Mr. Alving, what they ought to do. They ought to exercise self-restraint from the first; that is what they ought to do.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: That doctrine will scarcely go down with warm-blooded young people who love each other.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: No, scarcely!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Continuing.
How can the authorities tolerate such things! Allow them to go on in the light of day!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Confronting MRS. ALVING.
Had I not cause to be deeply concerned about your son? In circles where open immorality prevails, and has even a sort of recognised position--!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Let me tell you, sir, that I have been in the habit of spending nearly all my Sundays in one or two such irregular homes--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Sunday of all days!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Isn't that the day to enjoy one's self? Well, never have I heard an offensive word, and still less have I witnessed anything that could be called immoral. No; do you know when and where I have come across immorality in artistic circles?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: No, thank heaven, I don't!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Well, then, allow me to inform you. I have met with it when one or other of our pattern husbands and fathers has come to Paris to have a look round on his own account, and has done the artists the honour of visiting their humble haunts. They knew what was what. These gentlemen could tell us all about places and things we had never dreamt of.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: What! Do you mean to say that respectable men from home here would--?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Have you never heard these respectable men, when they got home again, talking about the way in which immorality runs rampant abroad?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Yes, no doubt--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: I have too.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Well, you may take their word for it. They know what they are talking about!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Presses his hands to his head.
Oh! that that great, free, glorious life out there should be defiled in such a way!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: You mustn't get excited, Oswald. It's not good for you.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Yes; you're quite right, mother. It's bad for me, I know. You see, I'm wretchedly worn out. I shall go for a little turn before dinner. Excuse me, Pastor: I know you can't take my point of view; but I couldn't help speaking out.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: He goes out by the second door to the right.
My poor boy!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: You may well say so. Then this is what he has come to!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: MRS. ALVING looks at him silently.
Walking up and down.
He called himself the Prodigal Son. Alas! alas!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: MRS. ALVING continues looking at him.
And what do you say to all this?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: I say that Oswald was right in every word.
units.name: MRS. ALVING
